independent_verification.own_extractor: I wrote my own scanner (single pass from index 0, tracking JSON string/escape state globally) rather than reusing the implementer's (which locates the first '{' and matches forward without knowing prior string state). Both were run over all 27,318 generated records.

findings.F1_extractor_divergence_none: ZERO divergences between my scanner and the implementer's across all three arms (zs 0, fs 0, qa 0). The brace-matcher bug the brief invited me to find does NOT materialise on this data. Honest negative result: the matcher is correct in effect here, though only incidentally — it is correct-by-data, not correct-by-construction. The ADR must specify the algorithm precisely and should adopt the from-index-0 scan, which is provably correct.
findings.F2_brief_numbers_use_a_looser_schema_tha: MATERIAL EVIDENCE CORRECTION. The brief's reproduce script checks only isinstance(d, dict) and isinstance(d['arguments'], list). The frozen parser additionally applies pydantic strict=True, extra='forbid', and duplicate-key rejection. Measured under REAL parser semantics: ZS extracted 8,959 (brief: 8,965, -6); FS extracted 9,105 (brief: 9,105, no change); QA raw 9,085 (brief's 'strict' column: 9,091, -6). The brief's QA headline '9,091/9,106 (99.8%) structural validity' overstates what parse_generated_frame accepts — the true figure is 9,085 (99.77%). Every figure must be restated under real parser semantics in the ADR.
findings.F3_template_echo_false_accept_probed_and: The frozen prompt template (docs/gate0/prompt-template.md) contains two literal JSON objects — the schema example (with role '<allowed role>') and {"arguments":[]} — so a template echo was a concrete silent-false-accept path (an echoed empty object is schema-valid AND grounds trivially, yielding an accepted empty frame). I probed it directly. ZS: 46 records whose first object is {"arguments":[]}, of which 0 have a competing later object. QA: 452, of which 0 have a competing later object. Longest ZS preamble is 1,076 chars and still has 0 later objects. The schema-example echo ('<allowed role>') appears as a first object 0 times in all arms (and would fail safe anyway via the parser's unknown_role check). CONCLUSION: the risk is real by construction but does not materialise in this data.
findings.F4_FS_later_objects_are_fabricated_conti: FS has 2,887 records whose first object is {"arguments":[]} and 2,879 of those do have later objects — but the later objects are numbered-token artifacts of the fabricated next example (e.g. {"i": 0, "t": "The"}), not alternative answers. The first object is correctly the model's answer.
findings.F5_extraction_is_a_strict_no_op_on_QA: Of the 9,085 QA records valid under both raw and extracted parsing, the parsed content is IDENTICAL in 9,085 and different in 0. Uniform application therefore does not perturb the untreated arm. This is the strongest single fact supporting uniformity.
findings.F6_empty_frame_asymmetry_THE_KEY_HAZARD: Post-extraction empty-argument frames: ZS 46/8,959 (0.5%), QA 452/9,085 (5.0%), FS 2,887/9,105 (31.7%). An empty frame is structurally valid AND passes grounding trivially (no spans to validate), so it flows through to acceptance as a contentless prediction. FS's certified acceptance can therefore be inflated by a large mass of empty predictions that say nothing. This is NOT caused by extraction (the empties are the model's actual greedy output and regeneration would not change them) but extraction makes them countable, so it must be controlled downstream.
findings.F7_gap_quantification_including_sign_cha: Structural-valid counts — strict: QA 9,085 / ZS 0 / FS 0 (gap +9,085 vs both). Extraction: QA 9,085 / ZS 8,959 / FS 9,105, i.e. gap vs ZS +126 and vs FS -20 (FS SLIGHTLY EXCEEDS QA). On content-bearing (non-empty) frames the picture inverts again: QA 8,633 / ZS 8,913 / FS 6,218, i.e. gap vs ZS -280 and vs FS +2,415. EXPLICIT ANSWER TO THE BRIEF'S QUESTION: yes, the ruling changes the sign of the structural-stage gap for FS. The strict +9,085 gap was a pure harness artifact, not a model-quality signal; but the post-extraction structural metric is near-saturated for all three arms and no longer discriminates. H1/H2 must therefore rest on grounding and certified acceptance, with empties reported separately.
findings.F8_ZS_non_closures_are_the_cap_not_rambl: All 140 ZS records with no closed object have finish_reason='length' with output_tokens exactly 256 (min=median=max=256). They are cap-truncated mid-object, not degenerate rambling. They are unrecoverable from saved output and remain structural failures under adopt — a residual harness artifact that this policy cannot fix. FS: 9,106/9,106 finish_reason='length' (confirms the missing stop sequence). QA: 9,106/9,106 'stop' (clean); its single non-closure is finish_reason='stop' at 89 tokens — a genuine model failure, not a cap artifact.
findings.F9_context_overflow_identical: The 18 context_overflow instance_keys are set-identical across all three arms (zs==fs==qa). The comparison's validity precondition holds.
findings.F10_grounding_unaffected: Extraction changes only the structural stage. For ZS/FS the raw output never parsed, so grounding never ran; extraction enables it. For QA the extracted object is byte-identical in parsed content (F5), so no grounding outcome changes. No grounding outcome is altered by this policy.

ruling_1_rationale.why_not_strict: Indefensible. It would report FS at 0% structural success when the model emitted a correct JSON object first and the harness discarded it for want of a stop sequence. CLAUDE.md's honesty boundary forbids presenting plumbing artifacts as extraction quality; strict does exactly that in reverse.
ruling_1_rationale.why_not_regenerate: Under greedy decoding (temperature=0) the tokens forming the first balanced object are identical whether or not a stop sequence halts generation afterward, so extraction from saved output is equivalent to regeneration for the recoverable mass — and I verified the preconditions rather than assuming them (finish_reason patterns consistent with greedy; extraction a strict no-op on the untreated arm). Regeneration is a LEGITIMATE upgrade and would additionally recover the 140 cap-truncated ZS records (1.5%), which adopt cannot; if Ross prefers maximal evidentiary cleanliness for ~$3-4 that is a defensible spend. It is not REQUIRED, and note it would NOT fix the F6 empty asymmetry.
ruling_1_rationale.why_adopt: The post-hoc concern is real and I weighed it seriously. It is answered here by properties I verified empirically, not by assertion: the transformation is uniform, deterministic, provably a strict no-op on the comparator arm (F5), preserves genuine failures (140 ZS + 1 QA stay failures), and corrects a documented harness bug rather than a model property. The degree of freedom pre-registration exists to remove is closed by the no-op + uniformity result.

binding_conditions: C1 — Restate every figure under REAL frozen-parser semantics (F2): ZS 8,959 / FS 9,105 / QA 9,085. The ADR must not carry the brief's loose-proxy numbers, and must state that the structural check is json.loads + duplicate-key rejection + strict pydantic (extra='forbid').

C2 — Specify the extraction algorithm exactly in the ADR, and use the from-index-0 global-string-state scan (provably correct) rather than find-first-brace-and-match (correct only incidentally on this data, per F1).

C3 — Report empty-argument frames as a separate, first-class column in every downstream table (ZS 0.5% / QA 5.0% / FS 31.7%). Certified acceptance must state explicitly how an empty prediction is scored against empty vs non-empty gold; FS's acceptance must never be reported as a single number that conflates 2,887 contentless frames with content-bearing ones (F6).

C4 — Disclose in the ADR that the policy was discovered and chosen post-hoc, after the run, with the harness bug (no stop sequence; 256 cap) named as the cause, and record that the pre-registered artifact was the strict parser.
C5 — Disclose the 140 ZS cap-truncated records as an unrecovered residual harness artifact (F8), not as a model failure; they remain structural failures.

C6 — Record in the ADR that the structural-stage gap for FS changes sign under this policy (F7) and that H1/H2 must therefore rest on grounding and certified acceptance, not structural validity, which is near-saturated post-extraction.
C7 — Apply the policy to all three arms from one code path, with a test asserting the QA no-op (F5) so any future change that perturbs the comparator fails loudly.
ruling_2_rationale: REQUIRE. The probe was a planned control that crashed for a disclosed implementer reason (the child 4-bit load OOM'd because the parent vLLM engine still held gpu_memory_utilization=0.90 on a 24GB L4; the engine was never torn down). Descoping a planned control because it crashed is precisely the silent weakening an independent review exists to prevent. The residual it covers — vLLM-vs-transformers PARSED-OUTPUT parity — is made more salient by this ruling, not less: the whole evidence base is vLLM-generated text from which we now extract a first object, so if the serving stack perturbs output, both structural and grounding numbers inherit it. R2 proved fresh-process RELOAD equivalence only. At ~$0.30 against ~$6.6 remaining this is the cheapest insurance available on the entire Plan 2 evidence base. Fix: tear the engine down before spawning the probe, or run it as a standalone job so no parent process holds GPU memory. Paid execution still needs Ross's explicit approval per CLAUDE.md.
scope_note: This ruling covers the extraction policy and the serving-equivalence probe only. It does not re-open the Plan 2 PASS at 8e5a2c8, and it does not authorise Plan 3, any spend, or any sealed-label access.
